related_public_source_candidate_screens.citation: Hirschmugl B, Perazzolo S, Sengers BG, et al. Placental mobilization of free fatty acids contributes to altered materno-fetal transfer in obesity. Int J Obes. 2021;45(5):1114-1123. doi:10.1038/s41366-021-00781-x.
related_public_source_candidate_screens.relevance: Term-human-placenta nutrient-transfer mechanism comparator. The article distinguishes isotope-labeled maternal fatty-acid transfer, endogenous release, fetal-side appearance, placental uptake, and model-estimated parameters; it is not an embryo-support or continuous-gestation source.
public_evidence_seen: The article reports 15 perfusions (lean n=8, obese n=7); the main clearance comparison uses n=13 after one experiment in each group was excluded for a missing measurement at one time point. A distinct n=1 experiment is a model-prediction check.

Article figures present group-mean ± SD clearance time courses and a representative model-fit plot; the model figure marks the syncytiotrophoblast state as having no experimental concentration data and states that maternal-vein concentrations were measured only at 90 minutes.

The five-page publisher supplemental PDF was retrieved and visually checked. Supplementary Table 1 gives FFA-mix concentration summaries over 14 experiments; Table 2 gives quality-control summaries for 15 placentae, with pressure, pH and lactate means calculated over 90 minutes; Table 3 gives lean/obese group characteristics, including group-level birth weight and ponderal index.
Supplementary Figure 1 reports group-level calculated placental FFA uptake (mean ± SD; lean n=4, obese n=3). No run-specific uptake values or source rows are provided in that figure.

Methods describe repeated physiological sampling and instrument logging, and the article defines an uptake calculation from reservoir quantities at 0 and 90 minutes. The article and supplement do not expose machine-readable run-linked concentration rows, numeric per-run reservoir-volume/sample-removal history, or numeric blood-gas/pump/pressure logs.

The publisher page identifies CC BY 4.0. The exact supplementary PDF and its retrieval URL/size/hash are preserved in the ignored local source artifact. No table values were transcribed, no figures were digitized, and no author was contacted.

related_public_source_candidate_screens.citation: Eliesen G et al. Placental transfer of tofacitinib in the ex vivo dual-side human placenta perfusion model. Current Research in Toxicology. 2024;6:100149. doi:10.1016/j.crtox.2024.100149.
related_public_source_candidate_screens.relevance: Public descriptive observation candidate. The primary article reports three successful cotyledon perfusions from different donors, and the publisher supplement contains individual maternal/fetal concentration trajectories for tofacitinib at ten stated times. The methods describe estimating reservoir volumes at sample times, but the inspected public table set does not expose numeric run-level volume/removal histories or individual recovery totals.
public_evidence_seen: The publisher-linked 25.7 KB supplementary DOCX was retrieved directly from the publisher content host and inspected. Table S1 contains individual placenta-labeled fetal and maternal FITC-dextran concentrations, Table S2 contains individual placenta-labeled maternal and fetal antipyrine concentrations, and Table S3 contains individual placenta-labeled maternal and fetal tofacitinib concentrations plus a no-placenta control series.

Table S3 reports three placenta-labeled perfusions from three different donors at t=0, 1, 5, 15, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150 and 180 minutes. Concentrations are in nM; the no-placenta control is marked N/A at 1 minute. The article reports plotted group means ± SD from n=3.

Cycle 243's standard-library audit reconciles all 70 Table S3 observation keys, source lexemes, units, compartments and missingness fields against the pinned DOCX. The DOCX table stores literal text values (no formula/cache layer); all 69 numeric values match and the control N/A remains not_assessed. The machine check does not replace human transcription/source review. See artifacts/perfusion-intake-2026-10-10/eliesen-table-s3-source-reconciliation-cycle243.json.

Cycle 244 independently recomputes arithmetic mean and sample SD from the three placenta labels at each time. At 180 min the maternal summary rounds to the article's 35.6 ± 5.5 nM, but Table S3's fetal values (30.0, 20.1, 24.9 nM) yield 25.0 ± 5.0 nM versus the Results text's 24.8 ± 4.7 nM. Preserve the discrepancy; the figure was not digitized. See artifacts/perfusion-intake-2026-10-10/eliesen-table-s3-group-summary-cycle244.json.

Cycle 245 uses the same DOCX's antipyrine Table S2 as a column-mapping control. Both 180-minute maternal/fetal means and sample SDs round to the article's 36.9 ± 3.0 and 36.7 ± 1.3 µg/ml, respectively. This does not resolve the separate tofacitinib Table S3 discrepancy, and no antipyrine observations were imported. See artifacts/perfusion-intake-2026-10-10/eliesen-antipyrine-s2-endpoint-control-cycle245.json.

Cycle 246 checked official Crossref and DataCite DOI-relation routes: Crossref's relation object is empty and the exact DataCite related-identifier query returns zero records. The publisher lists only mmc1.docx and states the underlying data are available on request. This is bounded metadata coverage, not proof of dataset absence; no author contact was made. See artifacts/perfusion-comparability-2026-10-11/eliesen-public-dataset-route-screen-cycle246.json.

The article reports 61 ± 10% tofacitinib recovery from combined perfusates at 180 minutes and 74 ± 4% antipyrine recovery; these are group summaries, not individual-run recovery rows. The no-placenta control time course is a system-adherence check, not a per-placenta recovery measurement.

Methods state that remaining maternal and fetal perfusion volumes were estimated at sampling times to inspect fetal-side volume loss. Tables S1–S3 contain concentration values only; no numerical run-by-time reservoir volumes, sample-removal amounts, or individual recovery totals were found in the inspected article and supplement. The article's data-availability statement says data will be made available on request; no author contact was made.

related_public_source_candidate_screens.relevance: Public observation-intake comparator. It does not publish a machine-readable observation table or the volume/removal records needed for dimensional transport or mass-balance analysis.
public_evidence_seen: Publisher full text and seven-page article PDF were inspected; five of seven collected placentas met the reported perfusion criteria.
Fetal samples are described at 30-minute intervals over three hours for all five trials; maternal time series are reported only for Trials 4 and 5.

Figure 3 explicitly identifies missing antipyrine fetal samples in Trial 1 at 30 minutes, Trial 4 at 30 minutes, and Trial 5 at 60 minutes; Figure 4 reports fetal onabotulinumtoxinA results for five trials and maternal results for two.

The paper reports an approximate 40–50 pg/mL functional lower limit for the onabotulinumtoxinA assay and says fetal samples were below detection; this is a bounded non-detection result, not proof of zero transfer.

The publisher article/PDF routes inspected contain no explicit data-availability statement, no linked supplemental dataset, and no numerical timepoint-specific sample-removal or reservoir-volume history.

related_public_source_candidate_screens.relevance: Public human term-cotyledon perfusion source with concentration and loss-corrected mass-balance figures. It documents sampling-volume correction but does not expose the per-run time series needed to reproduce a dimensional balance.
